profile.summary: ProtRNA is an RNA language model made by adapting a protein language model, ESM-2, to RNA sequences. The authors' idea is that information learned from the much larger body of protein sequences can transfer to RNA, where sequences are fewer and less conserved. It takes RNA sequences and returns per-nucleotide embeddings, which the repository uses for secondary structure, protein-RNA interaction and mean ribosome loading prediction.

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: ProtRNA starts from the ESM-2 protein language model and is trained further on RNA by a cross-modality transfer learning strategy. In the released code the model keeps the ESM-2 vocabulary of amino acids and appends lower-case RNA tokens (a, u, g, c, x), so the same alphabet holds both kinds of sequence. Input RNA is lower-cased, T is mapped to u, and any other character becomes x. The pretrained model built by the loader has 33 layers, embedding dimension 1280 and 20 attention heads. Embeddings from layer 33 feed separate prediction heads for each downstream task. The sources read do not describe the RNA training objective or data in detail.

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: One pretrained language model is released, ProtRNA_pretrained.h5, as TensorFlow weights on Zenodo record 14795554. The same record holds task heads: four RotaFormer secondary structure heads trained on different datasets and selected under different metrics, protein-RNA interaction heads for 17 RBPs in HeLa cells, and a mean ribosome loading head (the last two in PyTorch). The README notes that an earlier version of the paper scored secondary structure with the authors' own metrics and keeps a script for that. A result should name the Zenodo record, the head file and the repository commit; this page read commit 991037d6. The preprint has two bioRxiv versions, and the bioRxiv record links a published version, DOI 10.1016/j.cels.2025.101371.

run_guide.summary: Create the conda environment, install the requirements, and compute ProtRNA embeddings for the README's three example RNA sequences.
prerequisites: conda, to create a python=3.9 environment.
numpy==1.26.1 and tensorflow==2.14.0 for base inference, from requirements.txt.
wget, which the loader calls to download ProtRNA_pretrained.h5 (2,605,079,184 bytes) from Zenodo into ./weights.
GPU need is not stated in the sources read. Code is Apache-2.0; weights are CC BY 4.0.

steps.title: Compute embeddings
steps.shell:
python - <<'PY'
from pretrained import load_pretrained_model

model = load_pretrained_model(name='ProtRNA_pretrained')
batch_converter = model.alphabet.get_batch_converter()

seqs = [
        "CAUAUCGUGAGAUGUGGGCGAGAAGAAGGGAUAGCGAAAUCGUAGCCCUACGGACAGAAACCUGAUAAUAAGGCGUGCAUGGCGGGUAAGUUGGCUUAAAGCAACGAAGCCCUAAAGGUAGCCGUAACCUAUGUGCGUAAAUUAGGAGGGUAGACGAGGAAAGAACACG",
        "AAAAGUUAAAAAUGAUAUUCCCGAAAGGAUGCACCAUGUGUAGAUGCCUUGUAACCGGAAUUGAAUGGGGGAAAAAGAAAUG",
        "AAGGUCGAGUGAUGAGCAAAAAUGCAUAGUUCAGAUGAUCAAACCCUAGUGGUUAUGAUUACUUUGAAUAAAUAGUCUUUCGCUCCUAACUGACGGCCUU",
]

seq_tokens = batch_converter(seqs)
results = model(seq_tokens, repr_layers=[33])

print("ProtRNA embeddings:", results["representations"][33])
PY
steps.explanation: The README's representation example, wrapped in a shell heredoc and run from the repository root so that pretrained.py can be imported. On first run it downloads the weights from Zenodo.

outputs: On first run the loader prints "Downloading weights for ProtRNA_pretrained" and "Loading weights ProtRNA_pretrained"; the script then prints the layer 33 embeddings for the three sequences.
